## 2026-11-03 — trade dialog prologue cascade blocked

`0x5B88B0` keeps 404 at object 4300 with frame 0x1368 and the first mismatch at 23, where native loads
the base into edx and we use ebp. The pass confirmed the earlier findings and produced no keeper. The
byte-typed prototype costs: `int __cdecl fcn_0050b750(int, unsigned char)` alone gives object 4290 with
match 238 and the same first mismatch, and adding `unsigned char*` for a0 gives 4291 with match 255.
Moving the top store to nSlots gives objects 4294 or 4295 with frame 0x136c and the base load in edi, and
pkt 0xfc brings the frame back to 0x1368. The blocker is the register cascade: on msvc-6.0-sp5-pp the base
load never reaches edx and exactly one of the five -1 stores is always sunk, whatever the source shape.
Tested: six store orders (plain, chained, declaration initialisers, struct temp plus copy, nSlots-1
sentinels, a shared negated variable, and all 15 scalars as a struct in native slot order with textual
field rewrite); ent spellings (void pointer, int, unsigned casts, operand order, the sibling 0x506380
form, two-step, register locals, base in tv, char pointer ent, unsigned sentinels); parameter and
prototype shapes; and pre-call uses or guards, all folded. Volatile is the only construct that forces
the stores but it emits `mov dword ptr [esp+..],0xffffffff` for eight bytes instead of a four-byte
register store: volatile hD with nSlots and pkt 0xfc gives frame 0x1368, object 4300, first mismatch 22
and match 428, the only candidate above 404, while volatile hA gives 4314, sel 4340, hB 4302, hC 4310
and all six 4367. The native cascade ent to eax, -1 to ebx, 0 to ebp and base to edx follows from -1
living in ebx, which only happens when the lea chain owns eax at materialisation time, and every source
form tested makes MSVC hoist the constant and take eax. A blocker is recorded on the row.

`0x5B7880` keeps 300 at object 4019 with the prefix at 0x4b; the counter pass produced no keeper and the

in memory at +0x08, pg at +0x04 and pIt at +0x00, and the byte-sum scratch in ECX precisely because EBX

cause: EDI stays free because f.win is never promoted, and our object touches frame+0x10 eighteen times
against native's seven. Rejected: rows-init on y or n (objects 4016, match 284 or 282, prefix still 0x4b
or 0x4a), because any genuinely zero-initialised fill index makes MSVC reserve EBX for i and evict the

and i; keeping i=4 entering the fill loop preserves 0x4b at 4016 and match 284 but is semantically wrong.

229 with ent in EDI and -1 in EAX, the same split already measured, so merged matches native's ent (EAX,
spilled) while split matches native's win (EDI) and neither gives both. A blocker is recorded on the row.

forced by liveness instead of a struct pad: hoisting

## 2026-11-03 — inventory dialog merge is register pressure, source clean

`0x5D0660` keeps its v14 state at 1258 with object 4389, frame 0x438, nine store blocks and lint clean; the
merge round produced no keeper and the source is byte-identical to kept-v14. The shared visibility block is
reproducible but the compensation pool cannot pay for it. The duplicate exists because of register pressure
rather than source shape: both tabB[2] arms already write identical statements, but native spills n3 to its
slot, freeing ebx and edi so the label text stays in a callee-saved register and the id index lands in esi at
both sites, while our build keeps n3 in ebx so the else arm reloads tabB[2].text and puts the id index in
edi, and MSVC's suffix merge therefore sees different register streams. Forcing n3 to memory reproduces
native's merge exactly, either as `volatile int n3` or through an address-taken use: eight store blocks, the
else arm jumping into the tabB[3] store tail at the native-relative spot, and the preludes `mov eax,reg; add
esp,0x10; shl eax,6; sub eax,reg`, with frame 0x438 held. Measured, all at frame 0x438: volatile n3 gives
object 4345 with eight stores and match 560; an address-taken n3 gives 4330, eight stores, match 430; that
plus eight sentinel conversions gives 4359, eight stores, match 556; a tabA[0] plus else sentinel variant
gives 4393 with nine stores and match 822; tabA[0] and tabA[1] reading .text instead of the temp gives 4359
with nine stores and match 376; and the volatile variant plus that tabA change gives 4335, eight stores,
match 392. The merge costs 33 to 44 bytes rather than 32, since the tabB[3] tail plus the else tail is 0x47
in native against 0x68 here, and the nine `cmp word ptr [mem],0xffff` sites are worth one byte each, about
14 in one build, leaving a merged object still 24 to 30 short with no byte-neutral compensation: volatile nb
or idx break the frame at 0x43c and volatile t0 gives 4538 while still merging. The rest of the deficit sits
in the tabA label blocks, where native stores .text before the branch and spills t0 and n3, and touching
those cascades through the allocation. The kept body has 1104 strictly equal bytes with the longest equal run
54 bytes at 0x154, so the match is spread over small runs and any global allocation change loses more than
the localized win. Recommendation: rebuild the pre-merge label blocks (tabA[0] and tabA[1], native
0x5d08e9..0x5d09cf, 17 and 6 bytes over ours) before landing the merge. Merged candidates are kept in
.scratch/660/r11/ (e1a and e10 are the cleanest at frame 0x438 with the shared block present), with tooling in
.scratch/660/tools/ and the write-up in NOTES-rewrite.md round 6.

1/1008, fcn_005c62c0 at 0.5 discount, the 60-worker loop, summe and anzahl, e->d4 times 0.9f, the
fcn_0050fdb0 0.25 blend, fcn_0050c830 differenz and the leistung blend); lager type 0x2a and 0x116; the
rohstoff four-word loop; the c8 message clear; the do/while production loop with its duplicated else-if
(produziert != 0 against e->c4 == -1); the mangel epilogue; case 2 and the -2/-1 loops; and the default.
Four load-bearing shapes were verified by build. `char bild[260]` rather than 256 gives `sub esp,0x724` with
text at 0x124 and debug at 0x524 exactly, where 256 gives 0x720. The early branch must place the
fcn_00546190 call after the if/else as a join, `if (short == 0xffff) { gebaeude = ...; if (gebaeude)
io_FormatTextBuffer(...); } else { switch (...) {...} } fcn_00546190(e);`, which makes the compiler emit
native's non-folded `add esp,0xc; push ebp; call; add esp,4` and the near je to the shared tail, while any
variant with the call inside the branch or with an early return folds the cleanups. The switch source order
must be case 1, case 0, case 2, case -2, case -1, which with case 0 present yields native's dispatch of
eax=value and ecx=index with the inline `inc eax` early return, while case 0 first or last or dropped swaps
the register roles and puts the early-return block out of line. And case 2 must be
`if (gebaeude) fcn_004c6300(...); else break; fcn_00546190(e); return;` so the zero path breaks to the shared
tail and the 6300/546190 pair stays unfolded. The largest remaining size gap is the `strcpy(bild, "...")`
inlining: native shares one 34-byte copy block across the ten ROHSTOFFMANGEL arms as `mov esi,literal; jmp
copy` around `lea edi,[esp+0x30]; mov ecx,8; rep movsd; movsw`, while our object inlines the whole copy per
arm in both chains for about nine bytes per arm, roughly 180 over. The same source shape shares in a
standalone translation unit, so the trigger is the surrounding block layout: native's chain falls through to
0x571c21 and ours jumps to a continuation at 0x44f because the arms are ordered differently, with native
laying out first-if body, final else body, else-if body and then the continuation. Also open: the FP ternary
where native loads `fld dword [0x6628a8]` for 0.0f and adds `[leistung]` while ours loads a qword 0.0 with
`fadd st,st(1)` and an extra `fstp`, plus a scratch slot at B+0x14 in native against B+0x08 in ours; and the
haushalt search loop where native uses `jl 0x85a0a0` and ours `jb`, likely from the comparison form of
`arbeiter < g_7f4ca0 + 768*0x21c`. Backup .scratch/he_RunProduktion.best.c holds the current source and
.scratch/norm.awk the normalised instruction diff.

ebp; divisions on left give obj, w, n; the 3921 baseline had w, leftw, obj, n for esi, edi, ebp, ebx; and
native needs obj, leftw, n, w. So w must fall from position two to last, below n, not merely below leftw, and
obj keeps esi because it inherits the register from the pre-loop walk at 0xa7b. Shapes measured inert for the
priority list with size and prefix held: a 16-bit-valued w, `unsigned short w` in a block, `short w`, w in a
nested block, renaming the loop w, renaming or splitting the early w, function-scope leftw in three
declaration positions, loop-head statement permutations (prefix 0xb0c or 0xb14), merged `left = leftw = ...`,
`75 * fcn(...)`, `2 * leftw / n`, `leftw << 1`, comparison operand order, hoisting w's definition out of the
gate block (the compiler sinks it back), a redundant `left = leftw` at the loop tail, using leftw after the
second loop (4414), splitting leftw into lwt at the second loop head, and swapping the [esi+1] and ent store
order. Making w memory-resident or inlined gives the wanted leftw in edi and n in ebp but deletes w's register
(4391 or 4400) or n's ebx, so it is not the answer. New native fact: fcn_0042e410 returns a 16-bit type, since
native emits `mov bx,ax; push esi; and ebx,0xffff; call; add esp,8; cmp eax,ebx`; declaring
`unsigned short __cdecl fcn_0042e410(int);` with `w = (int)(fcn_0042e410(0x5a) & 0xffff)` reproduces that
sequence exactly with the same scheduling but costs one byte for object 4394, which balances against leftw in
edi dropping the `+0x0` displacement that ebp forces on `lea eax,[ebp+ebp*1+0x0]` at 0xe17, so the role flip
and the 16-bit callee fix are both needed to hold 4393 and the role flip comes first. A role-normalised
structural diff of the loop shows the remaining non-register differences are only the scheduling of
`mov cl,[0x773d75]` with its and, the ENTCLASS encoding `[eax+ecx*1+0x247]` against native's
`[ecx+eax+0x247]`, and the [esi+1] load placement in the evs fill; the loop CFGs are identical with the back
edge at 0xb3b, so the colouring difference is not a CFG artifact. Artifacts: ROUND4.md with the full measured
table, roles.py, exp.py and xloop.py, plus keep_wret_tmp.c for the 4394 16-bit callee variant. Recommended
next attempt: treat the colouring as opaque and either find a shape that moves w below n, with the untested
family being a change to how n's 2/4/8 accumulation interacts with the divisor, such as accumulating a
multiplier instead of n, or accept the current roles and push on the remaining per-instruction differences.

is a register-role inversion, with the compiler putting the constant zero in ebp and spilling v10 to 0x18(%esp)
where native keeps v10 in ebp, the zero in ebx and the spill at 0x10; the cost appears at the join as

Five edits landed. The three array clears must be `memset(x, 0, sizeof x)` rather than `= {0}`, because `= {0}`
makes MSVC 6 store element 0 and then run a `rep stosd` of n-1 where native runs one full-count `rep stosd` at
0x7c, 0x4c and 0x174, and that alone moved the prefix from 0xa to 0x35. The counter n is a declarator initialiser
declared before kinds and emitted between the three memsets and the kinds byte block at native 0x512f12. The first
found loop needs `(int)` casts on both sides of the pointer-range compare so it emits `jl` as native does at
`cmp eax,0x85a0a2`. fcn_00598150's first argument is `name` and not `kind`, since native pushes
`lea edx,[esp+0x1b4]` then `lea ecx,[esp+0x214]`, and the prototype is corrected to `(char *, char **)`; this was
a real transcription error in the existing file. And the found-loop counter is merged into total with a separate
k for the 0xb to 0xd and g_6a3440 counters. Remaining gaps in rank order. The scalar slot permutation is
systemic: native has i at 0x00, count and total at 0x04 and inner at 0x08, while ours has total at 0x00, i at 0x08
and inner at 0x04, and docs/msvc6-allocator.md Finding 52 gives the rule that for same-size locals the j-th
initialised takes 0x0, 0x8 and 0x4 in sequence with declaration position irrelevant, so native's pool order is i,
inner, count against our count, i, inner; declarator-init order, statement-init order, renames and merging count
into total all leave it identical, and every reference to those slots carries a wrong displacement byte, which

## 2026-11-03 — inventory extents repaired where the reference tails are padding

Two extents were wrong because the inventory includes alignment nops that follow the function. Disassembly of
the reference ends 0x561380's code at 0x562184 with twelve 0x90 bytes from 0x562184 to 0x56218f, so its code
extent is 3588 rather than the inventoried 3600, and it ends 0x571870's code at 0x572758 with eight 0x90 bytes
from 0x572758 to 0x57275f, so that extent is 3816 rather than 3824. Both were repaired through
`rebrew binary repair-extents 0x561380=3588 0x571870=3816 --reason ... --sync-rows` after a preview digest of
cbd7f888f18a5d0d22da4c702e79fc7c4e570b803a0c14b0c605252db04caa81, which updated the inventory rows and synced the
function row sizes. The effect is direct and large: 0x571870 now measures 2757 matching bytes at object 3816
with size 3816, so its verdict moves from SIZE_MISMATCH to NEAR_MATCHING because the size is exact, and 0x561380
measures 1244 at object 3592 against the corrected 3588, so it is four bytes over its code extent instead of
eight. This also explains the earlier confusion where a row's object could never reach the inventoried size: the
object extent excludes trailing section padding that the inventory counts. Rows whose extent has not been
audited keep their inventoried sizes, and the same repair is the right step for any other row whose reference
tail is alignment padding.

## 2026-11-03 — extent audit classified, table tails included

The inventory audit found 151 rows whose recorded extent ends in a run of at least four 0x90 or 0xCC bytes. A
decode from each row start, resynchronising over validated four-byte jump tables, split them into 21 rows whose
code ends with a control transfer followed only by padding with the next row starting exactly at the recorded
end, 89 rows whose byte before the run is the last dword of an in-function jump table whose targets point back
into the row, and 41 rows that did not classify because of decode desync or a data tail, which stay excluded.
The classification table is .scratch/extents/classified.json. Both of the first two classes are repairs: the
criterion is that the trailing run is alignment after the function's last content, and for a switch-bearing
function that content is the jump table. The earlier filter wording that required the byte before the run not to
be table data was wrong and would have excluded the two precedent repairs, since 0x561380's table dwords end at
0x562184 with twelve nops to 0x56218f for an extent of 3588 and 0x571870's dwords end at 0x572758 with eight nops
to 0x57275f for 3816, both of which were applied. Multi-byte nop forms also count as padding, so the row
0x641810, recorded at 368 bytes with a 32-byte int3 run and a 7-byte `lea esi,[esi]` between the final ret and
that run, is repaired to 329 rather than 336. Repairs run in batches of at most eight through
`rebrew binary repair-extents 0xVA=SIZE ... --reason <evidence> --sync-rows`, with a dry run for the input digest
and then the apply guarded by `--expected-digest`, and receipts kept under .scratch/extents/.

## 2026-11-03 — crew dialog frame needs expression pressure, not declarations

`0x43C640` keeps 469 at object 5169 against native 5419 with the frame at 0x54 and the first mismatch at offset 5
where native is 0x60; the frame pass kept nothing and the source is restored to the session baseline. The tactic
of naming the two H-derived temporaries cannot work as stated: MSVC sinks a standalone `hh = t->H; hx = hh*x;`
past the following call and rematerialises `[ebx+4]` afterwards, so the named values never become live across the
RNG call and never claim slots. The frame only grows with expression-shape pressure, not declaration count, since
three unused ints leave the frame at 0x54. Measured probes, all kept as evidence and reverted from the source:
hoisting H, hx and hy before all sixteen RNG calls gives frame 0x58 at object 5335 with match 447; adding
`hz = hx + col` gives 0x5c at 5312; moving the RNG call inside the verts expression as
`... + (f = (float)fcn()*g*jx) + f ...` gives 0x58 at 5360; and volatile hh, hx and hy gives 0x5c at 5856, over
native's size. None reached 0x60 and every one lost match, so all were reverted. Two further differences were
recorded that bear on the same region: native emits the record-init loop as direct stores at material offset +0xbc
over eight strides of 0x34, where our source walks a RegionRecord pointer from +0xa0, and native's memset form
emits three rep-stos stages against our two. Both change register pressure in the region that owns native's -0x58
and -0x5c slots, so the next lever is to reproduce the region-init and scan expression shapes, namely the memset
length temporaries, the direct material-field stores and `off` held in a slot, rather than forcing the emission
temporaries. Backups in .scratch/goldtl-0043c640/ with v4-hoist.c, v5-comma.c and v6-volatile.c.

## 2026-11-03 — quest dialog low pool is claimed by address-taken-ness

`0x512EE0` keeps its state at 393 with object 3448, three relocations, frame 0x404 and lint clean; the slot pass
kept no edit. The mechanism is now known: the low pool slot is claimed by address-taken-ness, not by declaration
or emission order, since declaration permutations of inner, total and i, renames and alternate initialiser orders
are all byte-identical. Taking the address of the value that must live at 0x14 moves the prologue store there,
which matches native: its only scalar lea site is 0x13375 for `&[esp+0x14]`, and native slot 0x14 is both the
found counter and the 0x65 and 0x69 count, because native stores the fcn_0050cf50 result straight to 0x14 at
0x13367, so native merges count into the found counter and keeps no separate count variable. Measurements, all at
frame 0x404 unless noted: making both address-taken sites `&total` puts the store at 0x14 with i at 0x10, gives
total 0x14, kinds 0x18 and prefix 0x2, but its semantics are wrong at 0x65 because total does not yet hold the
fcn_0050cf50 result; splitting the sites, first `&count` then `&total`, keeps frame 0x404 and kinds 0x1c with i at
0x10, total at 0x14 and count at 0x18, and raises the prefix to 0xe9 with match 405 at object 3469, but native's
two amp leas at 0x13375 and 0x13389 both resolve to slot 0x14, so that split cannot be the original shape and is
not promoted; and the correctly merged forms, whether by renaming count to total or merging it, are semantically
right but drop i from the low pool with frame 0x400, kinds 0x18 and prefix 0x2. A third artificial address-taken
scalar restores frame 0x404 but still leaves kinds at 0x18, so the third low slot appears only when the third
scalar is itself address-taken, which native's lea inventory rules out. The conclusion is that i at 0x10 and total
at 0x14 are reachable by making total address-taken, while the third slot, inner at 0x18 in native, is a plain
register spill, and our merged-correct shape does not spill inner because our do-while register pressure is lower

## 2026-11-03 — crew dialog frame reaches native width

`0x43C640` keeps the widened frame at 0x60, exactly native, with the prologue matching through offset 6, object

produced it: the record-init loop writes the material field directly at +0xbc through an int pointer with a 0x34
stride over the eight strides and the count2 loop advances that same pointer, matching native's
`lea 0xbc(ebx,eax); movl $2,(eax); add 0x34,eax; dec/jne`, where the older `r->material` form emitted
`mov [ecx+0x1c],2`; `hh = t->H` and `hx = hh*x` are hoisted before each of the sixteen RNG calls with hx used in
the verts index, matching native's -0x10 and -0x14 slots and its H*x reload after the call; and `cells = t->H*t->H`
is a persistent local used at the memset of cand, the bestmap memcpy and the memset of map, which is the pure-C
shape that buys the third frame slot. Three findings shape the next pass. The three-stage rep-stos clear cannot be
produced from C on this profile, since ten spellings under the sp5-pp driver give the plain two-stage form, which
agrees with docs/msvc6-c-shapes.md section 11 and docs/codegen-walls.md section 6b, so native's -0x58 store and its
separate fild temp at -0x60 need reviewed assembly if they are wanted. `off` already owns a slot, so native's

`0x5744C0` stays at 1246 with object 3980 against native 3976, 51 relocations and the first mismatch at 0x27;

reference v15 0x10, v21 0x14, v13 and v29 0x18, v30 0x1c, v17 0x20, v20 0x30, v36 0x40, v16 0x44, v18 0x98,
v19 0x11c and v22 0x19c, so there are two pair swaps plus a difference in v13's home. Layout levers exist but
cost bytes: `char v20[16]` instead of `[14]` packs the two-byte pad and flips the aggregates exactly to v16 0x44
and v18 0x98, as does a store to v16 or removing the case-7 clear of v18, yet the result is object 3992, table
0xf70 and match 1008, because the 0x985f0 lea drops from seven bytes to four while each of v18's two
`lea [esp+0x98]` sites grows from four to seven, so case 7 goes plus six, case 8 plus six, case 9 plus fifteen and
cases 0 and 1 plus fifteen. Declarations, element type, alignment and struct grouping are all irrelevant to the
pair order. The stronger root cause is that the frame order is downstream of where v13's home lands: the
reference keeps v13 in ebx across case 7 and spills its home only after v29 dies, so v13's home aliases v29's
slot, with the spill `mov [esp+0x18],ebx` at 0x57494b and the float store `fst [esp+0x18]` at 0x5748f5 sharing
0x18, v13's zero-init store `mov [esp+0x18],ebx` at 0x57486d, and v30 at 0x1c, while our build homes v13 at 0x30
shared with v36 and spills there at 0x48a. A volatile read through `*(volatile float*)&v29 = 0.0f` forces the dead
init store but leaves v29 at 0x1c, so that lever does not move the pair either. The remaining route is to
reproduce the reference's allocation order for v13 and v29 from case-7 code shape, or to accept the frame order as
downstream and chase the four-byte overage through case 8 and case 9 scheduling, which are minus ten and plus nine
today. The round also added .scratch/row5744c0/frames.py, an authoritative slot dump through /FAs, plus slots.py
and the exp variants A_swapdecl, B_v16int, C_v18char, E1_noloop, E3_v16store, H_v20_16, H_v20_12, S1_aggs,

## 2026-11-03 — inventory switch case six merge tied to the minus-one register

`0x561380` keeps its state at 2451 with object 3584 against native 3588, 110 relocations and lint clean; the
case-6 pass kept no edit and the source is byte-identical to the v29 state. Case lengths remain 0xd8, 0x5a, 0x86,

`or ebx,-1` (0xcb). The main finding is that the case-6 tail merge is not independent of case 3 but rides the same
knob as the minus-one register. Because the v29 state hoists `q = p + 0x52` above the fcn_004f4f60 call, q takes
edi across that call, r takes ebx, and the function's -1 constant is forced into ebp; with -1 in ebp the fail block
at 0x10f, which is case 0's tail, is `mov %ebp,0x70` plus the epilogue and is byte-identical to case 6's own r==0
return at 0xd42, so every fail goto including case 6's else is redirected there and case 6's je becomes the
two-byte short form for 0x7c. Every variant that leaves -1 in ebx instead gets case 6 at 0x80 with the six-byte
far je, because the canonical fail block at label_561d51 inside case 5 then starts with `or $-1,%ebx` and is not
identical to case 6's copy, so nothing is redirected: breaking the merge is the same thing as moving -1 to ebx.
The best lead measured, c3i1 in .scratch/r561380, advances the parameter destructively instead of using a q
register, `a0 = (void*)((unsigned char*)a0 + 0x52);`, which gives case 3 at 0x121, case 6 at 0x80 and -1 in ebx,
but case 5 grows to 0x47f for object 3592 and match 2315, below the current state, so it was reverted and its
first mismatch moves from offset 17 to 43. Case 5 grows because native zeroes ebx with `xor %ebx,%ebx` at 0x561cf8
since ebp holds v10, so the zeroing also kills -1 and label_561d51 becomes the seven-byte `movl $-1` at case-5
offset 0x11e for 0x47c, whereas in our builds v10 spills, ebp is free, the zero goes to ebp, ebx keeps -1 and the
fail block becomes `or $-1,%ebx` plus a late `mov %ebx,0x70` at offset 0x257 for three extra bytes. Forcing v10

so the -1 register is never clobbered there, and cases 4 and 5 get `movl $-1` only because their bodies reuse that
register before the fail. The next step is to make case 5's zero constant land in ebx while -1 stays in ebx, which
native achieves by keeping v10 in ebp. Variants c3i1, c3h1, c3g2, c3e1, c6m2, c3t1, c5v10, c3j1, c3j2 and c3j3

the rd_object definition under a narrow authorization for this one row. The four-byte cause was structural: the
reference is 3348 bytes made of 3276 bytes of code ending in the `ret` at 0x447ddb followed by 72 bytes of jump
tables at 0x447ddc and 0x447e00, while the previous object was 3352 bytes made of 3277 bytes of code ending at

the tail inner loop, where the source inlined `*(char**)(RD_DRAW(object)+off+0x410)` and MSVC therefore reloaded
[ebp+0x1ec] for six bytes and recomputed `[eax+ebx+0x410]` for seven bytes on every iteration, where native hoists
the list pointer into esi once and indexes with `mov ecx,[esi+eax*4]` for three bytes. Hoisting that pointer into a
block-local `char* entries` inside the for body, assigning it once from the same expression, and indexing with the
existing `type` variable makes the code 3276 bytes, aligns the tables at 0xccc, and removes the pad, so the object
is exactly 3348. The remaining 34 differences are all same-size encodings, 32 inside the RD_LIGHT_NINE region at
offsets 1638 to 1800, 2186 to 2270 and 2489 to 2762, where the base and index order in the SIB byte and one store
order differ, and two in the tail at offsets 3182 and 3189 where we emit `mov ecx,[edx+ebx+0x40c]` and
`lea eax,[edx+ebx]` against native's `[ebx+edx]`; flipping the source operand order for those addresses produces
identical bytes, so they appear to be encoding decisions rather than source order. One metadata mishap is recorded
here because it was repaired: testing another address against this file wrote the rd_object size and source hash
into the neighbouring row 0x447e30, which was restored from the committed store and then rd_object was re-promoted

displacement is real; and section metadata noise, with 173 rows declared .bss whose reference VA is .data, 13

placement through the `_dlead_<tu>` mechanism that `rebrew data layout converge` adjusts, premised on
`rebrew data layout audit --section .data --json` listing this target's objects, then emitting the 46 read-only rows

client target's objects entirely, listing only bss_late.c.obj which is not on the TL link line. No metadata or
source change was made by this diagnosis.

## 2026-11-03 — read-only data rows must come from the stub generator

The 46 rows whose reference VAs lie in `.rdata` while their owners emit into `.data` cannot be fixed by editing
their definitions: every owner lives in stubs/goldtl/symbol_stubs.c, whose header states it is auto-generated by
`rebrew build symbol-stubs` and must not be edited by hand, so a manual const qualifier there would be overwritten on
the next regeneration. The decision is therefore to treat it as an upstream generator gap: `rebrew build

managed declaration is const-qualified, while leaving `.data` and `.bss` rows and any written symbol alone. The fix
is being made in the upstream checkout at /home/maci/Desktop/Projects/relumea/repos/rebrew with a regression test
that shows a `.rdata` row producing a non-const stub before the change and a const one after, followed by
regenerating the scaffold in this project and re-measuring `.rdata` placement. No scaffold or generated file was
edited by hand for this step.

## 2026-11-03 — production message float compare block parked

`0x569FF0` stays at 982 of 3772 with the object exact and lint clean; the evaluation-order pass kept no edit and the
source is byte-identical to the 982 baseline. Native's target block at 0x56a84e is
call gm_RandomFloat01; fld [esp+0x10]; fld [esp+0x20]; fmul qword [0x665ed0]; fsubp st(1); fst [esp+0x10];
fcompp; fnstsw ax; and eax,0x4100; jne; mov [esp+0x14],1; jmp; mov [esp+0x14],0, which is 58 bytes, while the
baseline at 0x82a does fld; fld; fmul; fsubp; fstp; call; fcomp; then test ah,0x5; jnp for 56 bytes. Four findings
explain why source cannot bridge them. A plain store cannot emit the non-popping `fst`, because fv is dead after the
comparison, so the compiler fuses `fv = fv - prod` into the compare and drops the store; only a volatile store, or a
store to a slot that stays live, forces it. The `jne` polarity is reachable only through the negated condition
`!(fv > rnd)`, since the forward condition emits `je` with a hoisted store. The `mov 1; jmp; mov 0` body is not
produced by this compiler for a two-simple-store if-else, which always merges into one hoisted store plus one
conditional store, so native's block is two bytes longer than ours and the case-5 tail sits 36 bytes ahead of native,
meaning exact sequence content cannot add matches and only a two-byte length delta could shift downstream. And the
same source under msvc-6.0-sp5 without the processor pack gives 724 at object 3788, so the `and eax,0x4100` forms are
not a wrong-profile artifact and the processor-pack profile stays correct. The only probe that reproduced call before
subtraction plus `fst`, `fcompp`, `and eax,0x4100` and `jne` in order at object 3772 was match-neutral and needed a
fabricated volatile qualifier, so it was rejected under the restore rule. A blocker is set on the row. Probes and
results in .scratch/569ff0/ including varA, varF, pr_p, sw_, wv_w1_0, s2, y1 to y3, z2, z3, t_A, t_s2, t_w1,
t_plain and t_final_r3.

## 2026-11-03 — terrain object SIB base rule closes twenty-five bytes

`0x447110` rises from 3319 to 3339 of 3348 with the object still exactly 3348, 114 relocations and status
NEAR_MATCHING; nine byte differences remain and lint is clean. The root cause of the SIB swaph was found and it is a
rule: MSVC 6 keeps the loaded pointer as the SIB base when the address uses a byte-offset accumulator such as
`lights + off + disp`, but keeps the materialised multiply register as base when the byte offset is written as
`index * stride` inside the address, which is why the RD_LIGHT_NINE copies already matched and the byte-offset
accumulator loops did not. Four loops were rewritten to the multiply form with identical address sequences: the two
lights loops use `RD_LIGHTS(object) + off * 0x38 + disp` with `off++` instead of `off += 0x38`, the light-fill loop
iterates `for (i = 0; i < 7; i++)` indexing `RD_LIGHTS(object) + i * 0x38 + disp` in place of
`for (off = 0; off < 0x188; off += 0x38)`, and the resource loop iterates `for (off = 0; off < 3; off++)` indexing
`RD_DRAW(object) + off * 0x4a4 + ...` in place of `for (off = 0; off < 0xdec; off += 0x4a4)`; iteration counts and
strides are unchanged and `off` is dead after each loop, so no value dependence changed. Twenty-five offsets closed:
1656, 1673, 1690, 1707, 1739, 1773, 1790, 2199, 2216, 2233 and 2250 for `lea` SIB swaps, 2489, 2505, 2521, 2545, 2558,
2570, 2583, 2596, 2612, 2628 and 2644 for light-fill store SIB swaps, 2762 for an inline strcpy SIB that closed as a
side effect, and 3182 and 3189 for resource-loop SIB swaps. The nine still open are pure instruction order: at 2186 and
2190 the stores `mov [esp+0x1c],esi` and `mov [esp+0x18],esi`, which are `left = count` and `start = count`, are
emitted in the opposite order to the reference, which writes left then start, and at 1638 to 1642, 1643 and 1647 the
first light loop schedules the induction variable `xor edi,edi` after our `start = count` store rather than before the
two stores. Source permutations that all produced identical bytes: swapping the assignments, a comma statement,
chained `start = left = count`, `start = left`, declaration-order swap, a for-init comma list, pointer and integer
domain casts, `(char*)off + disp`, array subscript, a named offset local and an unsigned counter. Reverting the first
lights loop to the byte-offset form would trade its seven SIB fixes for the five ordering bytes, so the multiply form is
the net win at nine rather than eleven. Sources in .scratch/rd_object/ with base.c as the pre-change state and expF.c as
the current one.

`0x5BA910` is not stub level, contrary to the earlier todo description: the body is a full transcription of 3413 native
instructions with 223 direct call sites and 92 distinct callees, every one of which has a project symbol, and the
blocker is whole-body register allocation rather than coverage. This pass kept edits that raise structural agreement
from 0.9883 to 0.9933 and mnemonic agreement from 0.6973 to 0.7024 while cutting the missing tail from eleven
instructions to one, and the byte match fell from 758 to 732 with the object from 12169 to 12137 against native 11948.
The trade is deliberate: byte agreement here is a longest-common-subsequence count over 3413 instructions that swings
by about thirty bytes per small scheduling change, so a faithful edit can lower it while fidelity improves. Four changes
landed. The status-message chain at 0x5baec2..0x5baf72 was rewritten from a jump-table switch to the native else-if
ladder over the `al` byte with the message ids 0x72f, 0x70f, 0x713, 0x717, 0x71b, 0x737 and default 0x70b in ecx, which
mirrors the native cmp al and je order and removes the ten trailing jump-table instructions. The same site carried a
real semantic bug: the third argument of fcn_00533dc0 was inverted, since native sets 0x73f when the flag is set and
0x741 when it is clear at 0x5baf49..0x5baf65, and the source had them the other way round. The entity loop compare at
0x5baabf became a zero-extending `*(unsigned short*)0x7746cc`, matching `xor ecx,ecx; mov cx,[edx]` rather than a
sign-extending load. The slot clear at 0x5bac98 was verified against the listing, three zero stores and four minus-one
stores followed by a three-iteration paired loop writing -1, and its in-iteration store order was left as the
better-encoding variant because reordering to native order cost 28 bytes of agreement. Two callees the body already
called were declared: `void fcn_0050de80(int, int*)` and `int fcn_005373e0(int, int)`, and a duplicate fcn_0046f740
prototype was removed. Unresolved call bindings remain for __chkstk, fcn_00466330, fcn_00472380, fcn_00502850,
fcn_0051af00, fcn_005462a0 and fcn_0064d41a, with another six outside the extent only because the object is 189 bytes
longer than native.
The first divergence is the saved-register sequence at byte 11. Native pushes ebx, ebp and esi, moves arg1 to esi,
zeroes ebp for the zero register, sets edi to minus one and uses ebx as the loop counter; this build pushes ebx, loads
arg2 into edx, pushes ebp, esi and edi, zeroes ebx, puts arg1 in edi and minus one in ebp, which is the same four roles
rotated by four cycles, and native holds 0x10 in ebx at 0x5bac9f where ours holds zero. Because the colouring depends
on per-pseudo benefit across the whole body, the next step is a matching pass on loop shape in 0x5bb419..0x5bbdd5 and
0x5bc240..0x5bcab6 rather than more transcription, and a continuation is doing that.

bytes are modelled twice. The defect is therefore not a wrong pad VA but a pad span over bytes that are already
emitted. Grouping the 128 pads: 13 are fully redundant for 1,990,600 bytes, 115 are partly redundant for 14,832,761
bytes of which 3,147,018 bytes are proven redundant while the remainder stands for reference zero fill nothing else

of 7,541,760, and 2,404,142 bytes cannot be attributed per pad because 3,982 defined globals have no reference VA and
the scaffold source is smaller than the linked symbol_stubs.c.obj. A robust lower bound independent of object sizes is
the pad-to-pad duplication of 1,990,012 bytes plus 1,125,492 bytes of overrun past the next modelled row, which is
3,115,504.

to 32, _dpad_9b0e20 from 36,896 to 16, _dpad_14ce8c2 from 94 to 30, _dpad_773de8 from 2,200 to 2,156 and _dpad_6b870c
from 728 to 696. The documented rule from the data-analysis skill and the ownership documents is that a pad is

string-copy fill stalls of the sitzung table, one after the `rep stosd` of sitzung[1] and five after sitzung[4]'s, at

## 2026-11-03 — terrain object nine byte ordering wall

`0x447110` stays at 3339 of 3348 with object 3348, 114 relocations and status NEAR_MATCHING; the pair-ordering pass kept
no edit and the source is byte-identical to the session start. Both remaining regions are pure instruction
permutations with no encoding difference. At 1638 the reference emits `xor edi,edi; mov [esp+0x1c],esi` for
`left = count` and then `mov [esp+0x18],esi` for `start = count`, while this build emits `mov [esp+0x18],esi;
xor edi,edi; mov [esp+0x1c],esi`, and at 2183 the reference writes left then start where this build swaps them. The
reference order equals the source statement order, and 19 compiles were byte-identical at nine differences: statement
swap, full reverse, `start = left`, a temporary local, an unfoldable expression between the stores, a pointer store
through `*(int*)(void*)&start`, a comma statement, a for-init comma list, declaration swap, combined declaration,
renaming, a long form, an unsigned form with a cast on the guard, a nested block, `do { } while (0)`, and a folded if,
each applied to the first loop only, the second loop only and both. Order is not globally forced, since the pair at
offsets 31 and 35 keeps descending source order in both images, and only this count-valued pair reorders. As a
diagnostic, deleting `start = count` from the first loop changed the size to 3324 and swapped the slot assignment with
start at 0x1c and left at 0x18 while the emitted order stayed start then left, so the earlier apparent flip was slot
renaming rather than an ordering change. With start fixed at 0x18, left at 0x1c and both stores sourced from esi, the
required order is not reachable from C within the allowed edit scope, and closing only the pair would leave the
`xor edi,edi` placement wrong, so it would not have been a kept improvement. A blocker is set on the row. Variant
matrix and details in .scratch/rd_object/NOTES-row-00447110.md.

## 2026-11-03 — largest row: colouring pass finds the loops already clean

`0x5BA910` rises from 732 to 750 matching bytes with the object at 12136 from 12137, against native 11948, status
SIZE_MISMATCH with 44 relocations and lint clean. One change was kept and four reverted. The kept change makes the
fill-loop calls pass the `a1` parameter instead of `f.v14` at lines 607 and 608, matching native's load of
`[esp+0x1864]` at 0x5bb463; that is worth 18 matched bytes and one object byte, and the same substitution in the release
loop at lines 561 to 565 lost 45 matched bytes and added six object bytes because the zero constant occupies the natural
register there, so it was reverted. The other reverted probes: adding the missing pointer dereference at the seven-loop
compare, which is native-correct but cost 31 matched bytes and two object bytes with no structural gain; splitting the
assignment from the call, which was byte-identical; writing the global as an indexed array, which was byte-identical; and
the release-loop substitution above. The saved-register sequence did not move under any probe and still emits
push ebx, `mov 0x1854(%esp),%edx`, push ebp, push esi, push edi and `xor ebx,ebx`, with arg1 in edi, the zero in ebx and
minus one in ebp, where native pushes ebx, ebp and esi, moves arg1 to esi, pushes edi, zeroes ebp and sets edi to minus
one.
Three findings reset the plan. Both named loop regions already match native in shape, so loop-shape edits have no defect
to fix: the entity and empty-slot scans at 0x5bb419..0x5bbdd5 are instruction-for-instruction identical with only the
counter register differing, and the outer slot walk with its inner three-slot loop at 0x5bc240..0x5bcab6 reloads and
decrements exactly as native does, so the divergence is colouring alone. The body spills more than native, with 771
against 718 stack memory operands and 139 against 119 large-displacement forms, which accounts for the 188-byte excess
better than any instruction shape and makes the size gap and the rotation the same symptom. And the first structural
cause of the rotation is the seven-iteration packet loop at native 0x5baa9f, where this build materialises
`0x14a56e8 - &f.vD4[0]` in a register with `mov $0x14a56e8,%ebp; lea 0xe0(%esp),%edx; sub %edx,%ebp;
mov (%esi,%ebp,1),%eax`, clobbering the minus-one register and forcing a second minus-one range at object 0x210, where
native uses `[esi+0x14a56e8]` with esi as `i*4` and keeps a single minus-one range from 0x5ba945 to 0x5bafc2; three
source variants on that loop produce byte-identical code, so the pointer base is the allocator's choice. The
recommendation is to stop treating the loop regions as the lever and work the 53 extra frame accesses instead, whose
first fixable case is making the seven-loop use native's index form. Backups in .scratch/5ba910/ with g_p1.c as the kept
state, base.c as the baseline and g_LEDGER.md as the probe ledger. A transient CatalogScanError from `rebrew diff`

## 2026-11-03 — upstream gap trace crash fixed

The `rebrew diagnose gap` crash found while working `0x519190` is fixed upstream in commit bf6a0bbe on the main branch of
the checkout at /home/maci/Desktop/Projects/relumea/repos/rebrew, not pushed. The traceback reproduced from this project
is `TypeError: cannot use 'bytearray' as a dict key (unhashable type: 'bytearray')` raised inside
difflib.SequenceMatcher's chain_b when `trace_gaps` builds the matcher at gap_trace.py:143. The cause is that capstone
exposes `insn.bytes` as a bytearray and the masked-key branch computed `raw[:1] + b"\x00" * (...)`; slicing a bytearray
yields a bytearray, and difflib uses those masked keys as dictionary keys. The fix makes `_masked_key` return
`bytes(raw[:1]) + ...` on that branch so every path returns bytes, and a review found no other dictionary key in the file
that could receive a bytearray, since `first_fault` and `_obj_text` key by integer and `_seq` uses the masked key tuple.
The regression test `tests/test_new_commands.py::TestGapTraceHelpers::test_diagnose_gap_keeps_bytearray_stream_hashable`
drives `diagnose gap f.c --va 0x1000 --json` through `rebrew.app.main` with compile and disassembly patched so both sides
carry an equal byte run, asserts exit zero and a structured payload with va, instruction counts and a null fault, and it
was confirmed to fail before the fix with the same TypeError. Verification: the exact failing command now exits zero and
prints JSON through the checkout CLI, the suite reports 13,730 passed with 29 skipped, ruff passes and mypy reports no
issues across 413 files, with pre-commit hooks passing on the commit. One caveat is recorded: the PATH executable at
/home/maci/.local/bin/rebrew is a uv tool install of release 6.16.0 and still carries the crash, and it was deliberately
not reinstalled, since the project uses its pinned environment rather than an editable checkout.

## 2026-11-03 — largest row parked on the colouring wall

`0x5BA910` keeps 750 at object 12136 with 771 stack operands against native's 718 and a saved-register sequence of
push ebx, arg1 into edx, push ebp, push esi, push edi and `xor ebx,ebx`, where native holds arg1 in esi, the zero in ebp
and minus one in edi. Five probes this pass all regressed and were reverted. Using the slot offset as a new local in both
three-slot loops took stack operands from 771 to 761 and big displacements to 121 but dropped the match to 735 at object
12178, because the frame grew from 0x1848 to 0x184c and every displacement shifted by four. Reusing dead locals instead
of declaring one gave an identical result, so the growth comes from extra cross-call liveness rather than the
declaration. The seven-loop byte-offset index kept stack operands at 771 and dropped the match to 717 at object 12200,
since MSVC then materialises two derived pointers. Folding `h` into the index was byte-identical, so `h` already shares a
slot. Dropping the `i` temporary in the slot loop raised stack operands to 779 and dropped the match to 733 at object
12255.
Three findings redirect the plan. The frame is exactly at native size 0x1848 with zero slack, so any value live across a
call costs a four-byte slot, and that shift is worth more than the ten stack operands it buys; introducing a local to
keep a value in a register cannot work on this function as modelled. The seven-loop is worth only about two of the 53
excess stack operands, because the excess is diffuse: 103 call-anchored windows differ and 80 of them have matching
instruction counts at plus one to plus four, so even a perfect seven-loop fix cannot move the 53. And a real defect was
found: the source uses `f.v9c` as a per-slot scratch at lines 1111 and 1383, while native never stores those values,
keeping the per-slot offset in esi across ten calls at 0x5bc8ce..0x5bcbf1, with slot 0x9c holding only the scaled offset
from line 484 that lines 1442 and 1446 read, so the loop writes also clobber that value. The fix is directionally right at
ten stack operands but blocked on freeing a callee-saved register. Address taking is not the lever either: `lea` with esp
is 64 in native against 69 here. The recommendation is to stop source-shape probes on this row until a register can be
freed. A blocker records all of this, including the unfixed `f.v9c` defect. Instruments in .scratch/5ba910/ with
s_probe.py, s_stack.py, s_align.py, s_region.py and s_pull.py.

## 2026-11-03 — identity rows for globals that had no reference address

A read-only derivation pass established which globals can be given a reference address from evidence and which cannot.
Inventory: 4,344 globals were scanned and 432 row names found, so 3,912 have no row, of which 3,775 are source-defined
and 137 declaration-only; the 3,775 split into 545 pad, lead and gap names whose VA is in the name, 3,202 scaffold stub
definitions and 28 real source definitions, with the stubs encoding 2,794 `.data` or `.bss` addresses, 268 `.rdata`
addresses, 6 `.text` addresses and 134 without a hex value. The audit's earlier figure of 3,982 is 4,344 minus the 362
globals whose name matches a row, so it counted declaration-only rows and treated names as having no VA.
The evidence route was tested rather than assumed. Anchors are the 3,233 map symbols with a known reference VA, 415 rows
and 2,818 name-encoded, and their emitted order disagrees with reference order in only 34 of 3,232 consecutive pairs, or
1.05 percent, but only 4 anchor runs have equal built and reference spans, which fixes just 6 interior symbols, while
2,639 interior symbols sit in unequal spans. Emitted order plus boundary VAs is therefore not sufficient, and the
structural reason is that pad piece starts were themselves computed as previous reference VA plus built extent, so pad
spans re-encode the same built extents and add no independent bound. What does work is the name encoding corroborated by
an exact fit, where the next encoded VA minus this VA equals the emitted extent: 936 objects pass, 738 `.bss` and 198 raw
`.data`, of which 197 raw `.data` ones are unique and collision-free and 155 have nonzero reference bytes that decode
consistently with the declared type. The ambiguous remainder is 1,865 encoded without an exact fit, 32 overlapping the
next anchor, 42 sharing a reference VA, 408 stubs without a `.data` hex, 28 real definitions and 23 absent from the map.
The convention applied follows docs/data-ownership.md line 39, which allows an unsized identity-only GLOBAL row to
record an address without asserting ownership, so rows carry `--kind GLOBAL`, name, size only where the exact fit proves
it, section and file, with no storage kind, backing or link symbol, and placeholder names stay. The first batch of 20 rows
was previewed with digest 2e9595fe7bf7b5e03f75055c4ab6849eddece9dd6280c14b03e3f48a64c117d6 and applied through
`rebrew data set --expected-digest`: 0x675308 as float 1.0f, 0x67530c, 0x675310 and 0x675314 as int -1, 0x67531c as
int 1, 0x675320 and 0x675324 as int 256, 0x677188 through 0x6771a0 as int -1 to -7, 0x678150 as float 1.0f, 0x678154 and
0x678158 as float -1.0f, 0x67815c as unsigned 5000 and 0x67a28c and 0x67a290 as float -1.0f. Lint passes after the write
with no errors and no new size, overlap or stale-evidence warnings. Two caveats are recorded: address rows do not move
`.data` VirtualSize, since only extents do, and only the 936 exact-fit objects have extent evidence; and these rows are
placeholder-owned, so `rebrew verify --data` must not be run against them because the built bytes are zeros while the
reference bytes are real, and they must never be given a storage kind of object.

## 2026-11-03 — d2 row two: block structure right, local set wrong

`0x4DCF50` keeps its state at 2495 of 8798 with object size exactly 8798 and 319 relocations, frame 0x7e0 on both sides
by `rebrew diagnose stack`, status STUB and lint clean; no source change was kept. Two corrections were measured and
reverted. Reordering the head statements to listing order made the handle and table store order and their frames match
native exactly, but the listing's two leading scalar zero initialisations, at frames 0x24 and then 0x14 between hnd[6] and
hnd[7], could not be reproduced, so the head stayed eight bytes short and everything shifted, taking the raw match from
1509 to 843. Slot probes that inserted `V = 0` for each declared variable were mostly dead-store eliminated, and the
survivors landed at 0x18 and 0x38 with none reproducing 0x24.
The recovered layout, with push displacements corrected, is msg at 0x40 holding state, f04, i08, f0c, text, id, pad and
hnd at 0x90, tbl at 0xb0, rec at 0x240 with rec.i[6] at 0x258, list at 0x370 and the entity argument at 0x774; the
object already agrees on msg 0x40, hnd 0x90, tbl 0xb0 and rec 0x240. The reason the body still diverges despite a
faithful transcription is measured, not guessed: direct call sites are 345 on both sides with an identical per-callee
multiset except sprintf and a call-order LCS ratio of 0.966, 329 of 345 in twelve blocks, while 278 of 319 rel32 operand
bindings conflict and only 41 validate, and the instruction-shape LCS is 0.402 with the largest run 11 and 40 of 2340
instructions equal. So block structure is right and instruction widths and operand displacements are wrong.
Two walls are confirmed. The frame wall is pre-existing, native 0x760 against an honest 0x6b4, and was not re-litigated.
The real blocker is the local set: native scalar locals occupy 0x14 to 0x38, twelve words, zeroed at 0x24 then 0x14,
where the source declares 33 scalars and the object puts attribution pointers at 0x3f0, so declaration-driven slots cannot
coincide. Body fidelity needs the native local set recovered first, with at most twelve scalars, because statement-level
edits cannot pay off before that. sprintf remains unresolved across nine call sites, since native target 0x64d41a lies
inside the declared D3DX8 external band and has no project definition; the prototype is declared as
`int __cdecl sprintf(char*, const char*, ...)` and reported rather than renamed. Details in
.scratch/004dcf50-findings.md.

## 2026-11-03 — text format buffer extent corrected, body verified faithful

`0x51AF00` keeps 888 matching bytes but its extent is corrected from 6464 to 6455, so the object now equals the
reference extent exactly at 6455 with 135 relocations and status STUB. The repair is evidenced directly: the function's
code and its selector table end at 0x51c836 and nine 0x90 bytes fill 0x51c837 to 0x51c83f before the next row at
0x51c840, so the code extent is 0x1937. It ran through `rebrew binary repair-extents 0x51af00=6455 --sync-rows` with
preview digest 8fe498984006afead8c8ee87e14b92fea2843ffa4a4994ed05708169f40575bd.
No source change was kept and the file is byte-identical to its pre-work state at sha256 1bc7857e. The wall is confirmed
rather than re-litigated: the third callee-saved register is unreachable, since native's prologue saves ebx, esi and edi
at 0x15, 0x18 and 0x1b for a check stack of 0x3338 minus twelve, while this build saves only esi and edi, so every local
displacement above the saved-register area is four bytes larger and matched runs collapse to accidental singles, of which
the only ones at least twelve bytes long are 0x221 and the selector table with its tail padding at 0x18e3. The object's
jump table at 0x188c and selector table at 0x18e4 both sit at native offsets.
Body fidelity was verified against the listing and no defect was found, reusing the earlier receipt. The call multiset by
project binding matches native exactly at 86 calls, including 23 sprintf, 22 fcn_0064d740, 10 and 9 of fcn_0042b2f0, 6 and
6 of fcn_00517b90, 6 and 6 of fcn_0051e070, 4 of fcn_00657a73, 3 __isctype, 2 fcn_0064d530, 2 toupper and one each of
0x500d60, fcn_004fe330, 0x50bc10, 0x517c00, 0x64eeec, 0x41d9e0 and 0x42e410, with the differing counts on fcn_0042b2f0
and ReportClientMessage being block duplication and rotation rather than wrong callees. The dispatch byte map decoded
from 0x51c7e4, base `%` with range 0x52, covers 22 cases C, S and s, i and I, T, w, f, v, F, u, U, b, B, e, E, N, a, D, G,
r and `%` with default 0x15, and this build emits the same 0x52 range and an identical 83-byte map. The 'G' seven-copy
chain with the 0x4800 split and suffix, the 'w' 0x8680b4 arithmetic with the 0x14a79c0 index, the 'D' call pair with the
0x14a5450 read, the 'I' argument order, the 'r' memset and random-mod sequence with its 0x6b7f98 bound, the 'a' sprintf
pair and the 'T' call were all checked and found faithful.
One real divergence was found and reverted because it moved neither metric: native compares the buffer bound unsigned with
`cmp ecx,0x17cb; ja` at six sites, while this build emits signed `jg` because the source casts `(int) strlen(...) + i`.
Dropping the six casts emits `ja` but leaves the match at 888 and the object at 6455, so it was restored under the
keep-only-improvements rule. A second measured experiment merged the two 'a' sprintf branches onto a shared insert, giving
match 872 at object 6459, and was also restored. Unresolved callees without project definitions are 0x64d530, 0x64d740,
0x64d41a, 0x64eeec, 0x64efb1 for __isctype, 0x64f367 for toupper and 0x657a73, all with declared prototypes, while all
nine project callees resolve. The tree already held the faithful j2 skeleton at 888 rather than an earlier 1027 receipt,
and that higher figure is accidental alignment rather than block-order fidelity.

## 2026-11-03 — d2 row: session loop lands and the colouring flips

`0x4DA690` rises from 1340 to 1488 matching bytes with object 7020 against native 7057, 73 relocations, frame 0x900 and
equal prefix 0x31f, status SIZE_MISMATCH. The key finding is that the eight spare bytes were never missing: `blkB.s98[4]`
was on the wrong side of `order[6]`. Native allocates s98 at 0xa8 to 0xb8 and order at 0xb8 to 0xd0, addressing
`[esp+idx*4+0xa8]` for s98 and `[esp+0xb8]` for the order scatter, while the source had order at 0xa8 and s98 at 0xc0.
Moving `s98[4]` out of blkB into blkA after `s54[3]` fills native's 0x9c to 0xb8 gap, puts every array base back, and
keeps the frame at 0x900 without adding or removing a byte. It also fixed the register allocation: a0 lands in ebx and the
zero in ebp, matching native's `mov al,[ebx+0x30]` and `lea edi,[ebx+0x34]`, where previous builds had them swapped, and
the equal prefix grew from 0x9e to 0x31f.
Anchors kept, with raw displacements: s98 at 0xa8, order 0xb8, sD0 0xd0, sF4 0x104, flug 0x124, sitzung 0x1e4, mid
0x304 and a0c 0x7fc, with `sub esp,0x900`, one epilogue and the loop tail `inc eax; cmp 6; jl 0x398`. The body from the
loop variant landed as well: the session loop is `do { s20 = order[s30]; ... } while (s30 < 6)` with s20 in slot 0x50 at
the fcn_004ea2b0 and `s20 - 1` and `s20 + 0x12a9/0x12bb` sites, the vote loop and arm io second argument is s34, the first
copy bound and dedupe scan bound are s0C, the dedupe block is `s4C = s0C` with base `0x9b0e24 + s0C * 0x35c` and outer
bound s44, and the per-row counter is s40. The escape set was retuned to blkA.s98, blkB.pad0, blkB.pad1, sF4 and the
scalars s0C, s10, s14, s18, s1C, s20, s24, s2C, s34, s40, s48 and s60, since other subsets give frame 0x904 or 0x8fc or
drop the prefix to 0x220.
Measured attempts, all with frame and order verified from fresh object compiles: the single-pass baseline is 1340 at object
7048 with order 0xa8, sixteen bytes low; the loop with six escapes dropped is 1326 at 7001; the loop with body fixes is
1253 at 7103 with frame 0x908; the s98 move alone on the baseline is 1346 at 7030 with order 0xb8 and prefix 0x31f; and the
landed combination is 1488 at 7020 with frame 0x900. Applying `s1C -= 1` per row measured worse at 1295 and was
reverted. Nearby alternates were 1493 at object 6984, 1476 at 7015 with 72 relocations and prefix 0x220, 1452 at 7026 and
1430 at 7028. Two caveats are recorded: the object is 37 bytes short of native because the per-row scene pass is still
about 538 bytes short, which is the round-one finding, and the row has 73 relocations against native's 72, one extra
address reference that the relocation-masked comparison tolerates. Kept copy in .scratch/4da690/r12_final_1488.c with
notes in r12_NOTES.md.

## 2026-11-03 — one hundred and forty more identity rows

A hundred and forty globals now carry an evidence-backed reference address, applied in five digest-guarded batches of
twenty-eight through `.venv/bin/rebrew data set` with a dry-run preview first, then the guarded apply, then lint and a
readback. The selection started from the 197 unique exact-fit `.data` candidates, minus the twenty already applied,
leaving 177, of which 140 passed every gate: exact fit to the next name-encoded anchor, a unique reference VA across all
candidates, clear of every existing row extent, a definition present in stubs/goldtl/symbol_stubs.c, a stub declaration
size equal to the emitted extent, and nonzero reference bytes decoding consistently with the declaration type. The batch
digests were baaa78a2c699d043bc3b3ddd70f88e69c2dac8acbf8206ad4e07f3bd6d22f38d for 0x006772bc to 0x0067d388,
3f4453759dbce94aabfffe0a9da97e0e8efd7211c782a8499b7ce395c50f1a65 for 0x0067d38c to 0x0067fca8,
b31d20b4759f343d6f0d27fdadcf053ef6749aaa8cc8987b246229d6ce93bff2 for 0x0067fcac to 0x006a2558,
09ef30eef546d506535f739b50bf5efb309a71e073df6abae752dc0cdcbf716a for 0x006a255c to 0x006a268c and
afdd27ed09b79addd96b926f0de093efcb652489396683e5a1bf649787b4e22e for 0x006a2690 to 0x006ad630. Lint after every
batch matched the baseline at no errors and the two pre-existing warnings, with no new data-shape warning, and no digest
guard rejected a batch. Readback returned changed zero for three rows per batch and for all 140 together, with store
digest c322325a20524f4ad48a3a0d52690960830dca57ba0457debc52e99f1eb7d3f7, and an audit of the store confirmed every row
is kind GLOBAL with a size equal to the emitted extent, section `.data`, file stubs/goldtl/symbol_stubs.c, and no storage
kind, backing or link symbol. The rows do not appear in `data_annotations` because identity-only rows carry no ADDRESS
anchor and the stub definitions sit outside src, so the changed-zero dry run is the authoritative readback. Size is the
emitted extent per row rather than a blanket four: most are four bytes but six are 1, 2, 16, 20, 112 and 232, and a
blanket four would have disagreed with those declarations.
Thirty-seven of the remaining 177 were skipped with reasons. Twenty-five have reference bytes that are entirely zero:
0x67bbfc, 0x67bc00, 0x67bc0c, 0x67bc10, 0x67fbb0, 0x6a3764, 0x6a3768, 0x6a9b94, 0x6ad580, 0x6ad628, 0x6ad62c, 0x6b5c2c,
0x6b5c30, 0x6b5c48, 0x6b5c4c, 0x6b5c50, 0x6b5c54, 0x6b5c58, 0x6b5c5c, 0x6b5c80, 0x6b5c84, 0x6b5c88, 0x6b5cb4, 0x6b5d08 and
0x6b5de4. Seven have a stub declaration size that disagrees with the emitted extent: 0x68a9cc declared int 4 against 16,
0x699396 unsigned char 1 against 2, 0x6a2574 1 against 4, 0x6a4758 1 against 4, 0x6a4760 2 against 4, 0x6a9b90 1 against
4 and 0x6b5df0 1 against 4. Three lack a definition in symbol_stubs.c, since flt_677684 and g_6b5dc8 live in
stubs/goldtl/data_scaffold.c and g_6b5dd4 has no file or type. One, 0x675318, already holds an identity row as
gv_00675318, and one, 0x6b5e08, has an extent of 512 that crosses the raw `.data` end at 0x6b6000 so no complete reference
bytes exist. A few applied four-byte identities land on ASCII-like dwords such as 0x6a2390 and 0x6a23b8, which is
acceptable because the rows assert address identity only and claim neither type nor storage kind. A further 431 `.bss`

## 2026-11-03 — palette guard corrected and a pointer dereference restored

`0x46C5A0` now measures 855 of 6080 with object 6072, 169 relocations, structural ratio 0.9696 and lint clean. Two edits
landed. The case 'F' palette guard at line 537 was `if (d < 9)` where native has `if (d == 9)`, which emitted a seven-byte
`jge 0x46d499` against native's two-byte `jne 0x46d4db` with the `and al,0xbf` path as fall-through, and the corrected
form emits `75 1d jne` with the same short encoding. The second edit is a correctness repair that costs match bytes: the
source read `g_1015ea4 = *(unsigned short*)(&g_772524 + 2)` with a local `extern int g_772524`, which takes the address
of the global slot and reads eight bytes past it, while native loads the pointer with `mov ecx,[0x772524]` and then
`mov ax,[ecx+8]`, and the symbol is declared and assigned as a `char*` elsewhere, in GOLDTL.fcn_00472880.c. The type is
corrected to `extern char*` and the read to `*(unsigned short*)(g_772524 + 8)`, which drops the positional match from 938
to 855 and moves the object from 6068 to 6072, and it is kept because a wrong memory read is not an acceptable trade for
matched bytes.
The remaining gap is the register and stack-slot assignment that the blocker names, confirmed rather than re-litigated:
the first divergence is at offset 12, native `push esi` against this build's `push ebx`, with native holding the slot in
esi, the zero in edi and the temporary in ebx where this build rotates those roles, and the prologue zero-store order and
a missing [ebp-0x34] spill follow it, while the palette frame base at -0x50 against native's -0x58 is a uniform eight-byte
shift with a faithful relative layout. A third candidate was measured in scratch and not applied: native re-reads
[slot+0x3c] twenty-two times where the source caches `t` and the object does it eight times, an inline-field variant gives
seventeen reads and a function end at 0x46dcb5 against native's 0x46dcac with masked equal bytes at 193 against 251, so
it trades match for size. Body statements were otherwise checked out against the listing: frame 0x6f8, the palette store
order, the '-' and '~' wrap search, the `cmp eax,0x4800` table indirection, the 3*span 'T' geometry, the call argument
constants and the `_isctype` and `1 < g_6b25b0` shapes. None of the sixteen game callees lacks a row, so no prototype was
added; the library calls are memset 0x64d530, strncpy 0x64d740, strchr 0x64e790, sprintf 0x64d41a, _isctype 0x64efb1 and
d2_GetResourceData 0x466190, and 17 relocations stay unresolved for lack of a project VA binding, with standard prototypes
kept and no header or store touched. Instruments in .scratch/g46c5a0b/ with patch.py, cmp5.py and the base and final
objects.

## 2026-11-03 — d2 two: slot table recovered, spill is the blocker

`0x4DCF50` keeps its state with object exactly 8798 and an unchanged source; the local-set pass reverted everything and lint
passes. One measurement caveat is recorded first because it affects every number on this row: at pass start the same
unchanged source measured 2495 with 319 relocations, and by the end it measured 2345 with 274, because shared managed
metadata changed under the pass, so binding-based masking moved. All variant figures were therefore taken in one
environment with a raw unmasked comparison, where the baseline is 1509.
The native scalar slot table was recovered from raw bytes. Slot 0x10 is the list-merge offset accumulator, addressed as
[esp+edx+0xe0] and [esp+edx*4+0x370], later reused for a handle freed at 0x4df0fc; 0x14 is the second head zero
initialisation at 0x4dcf74 and then the fsum float accumulator with `fadd` and `fstp [esp+0x14]` at 0x4dd5e7 and
0x4dd5eb, reused for a handle later; 0x18 is p34, the lookup of a0+0x34 stored at 0x4dd0df and live to the end; 0x1c is
p3c from a0+0x3c stored at 0x4dd10d; 0x20 is n, the return of fcn_004f5740 stored at 0x4dd0ca and used as a loop bound;
0x24 is the first body store at 0x4dcf65 and later the folter-result 0/1 flag at 0x4de4f2 and 0x4de5f4, read before the
didFolter test at 0x4de765, then reused for a handle freed at 0x4df11a; 0x28 is p40 from a0+0x40; 0x2c is p48 from
a0+0x48; 0x30 is the weight tbl.f[i] stored with `fstp` at 0x4dd00c and reused for temporaries; 0x34 is p44 from
a0+0x44, reused later; 0x38 is h2, the return of fcn_004e4ae0 stored at 0x4dd1c4 and freed at 0x4df0eb; and 0x3c is a
short-lived integer temporary at 0x4dd46e that is not live at the head. A correction to the previous pass: native keeps
p38 in ebx with no stack store, while our object spills p38 to 0x18, and that spill is the thirteenth long-lived stack
value against native's twelve, which is why the head cannot grow.
Seven declaration and head variants were measured and reverted. Reordering the head with a volatile xpad first and a new
volatile ypad after hnd[6] gives frame 0x760, object 8798 and raw 1109 with the first difference at 0x14; reordering the
head with the fsum and didFolter initialisations moved up and xpad deleted gives frame 0x764 and raw 1201 with the first
difference at 0x02; reordering with didFolter first and fsum after hnd[6] gives 0x764 and raw 983; removing xpad alone
gives frame 0x760, object 8791 and raw 886; reordering the pointer declarations with p38 last is byte-identical, which
proves declaration order does not affect slot assignment; declarator initialisers give 0x764 and raw 951; and fsum before
didFolter gives 0x764 and raw 919. The reason is that every variant producing the two head zero stores extends the fsum
and didFolter live ranges to the function top, and with the p38 spill already occupying the twelfth slot the frame grows
by four bytes, with `sub esp,0x764` and msg at 0x44 and rec at 0x244, so divergence moves to offset 0x02 instead of past
0x18. Removing xpad costs 623 matched bytes, so it is load-bearing. The recommendation is that the blocker is register
allocation rather than declarations: recover what native keeps in ebx, esi and ebp and why this compile spills p38, likely
one extra simultaneously live scalar, and once the spill disappears the two head initialisations fit without growing the
frame. Evidence and the variant table are in .scratch/004dcf50-findings.md with helpers in
.scratch/goldtl-004dcf50-tools/.

## 2026-11-03 — stub sizes corrected and thirty two more identity rows

Six stub definitions whose declared size disagreed with the reference extent are corrected in
stubs/goldtl/symbol_stubs.c, and 32 identity rows are recorded, including the 25 that were skipped only because their
reference bytes are all zero. The file's hash moves from 2215182f to 29b23529. Each edit changes only the length, keeping
the element type every caller already declares: `unsigned char g_699396[2]` where the declaration said one byte and the
extent is two, with reference bytes `ff 00` and a caller writing and reading one byte as a 0xff sentinel;
`char g_6a2574[4]` for a reference dword `01 00 00 00` used as a flag with a `!= 0` test; `unsigned char g_6a4758[4]`
for `ff 00 00 00` with a sentinel caller; `unsigned short g_6a4760[2]` for `ff ff 00 00`, a dword `0xffff` sentinel;
`char g_6a9b90[4]` for `ff ff ff ff` with its address taken with length two; and `char g_6b5df0[4]` for zeros, dereferenced
by its caller as a four-byte pointer slot. These six edits are provisional in the same way as the earlier const work,
since the file is auto-generated and its regeneration is deferred.
One candidate was rejected rather than changed: 0x68a9cc keeps its `int` declaration and its row size of four, because the
extent of sixteen is an anchor artifact. Bytes 0x68a9d0, 0x68a9d4 and 0x68a9d8 are the int stubs `cm_LastEntityId`,
`cm_LastBuildingId` and `cm_LastObjectId` in the same file, the map emits five symbols consecutively at 0x887374, 0x887378,
0x88737c, 0x887380 and 0x887384, and the reference bytes are two then -1, -1, -1 as last-id sentinels. Forcing
`char g_68a9cc[16]` was compiled and measured and moves `.bss` from 0x590d10 to 0x590d18 and g_68a9dc from 0x1705fc to
0x170608, swallowing the three counters and overlapping their rows, so it was dropped from the size-disagreement list.
The 32 rows were applied in one request with preview digest
c322325a20524f4ad48a3a0d52690960830dca57ba0457debc52e99f1eb7d3f7 and a guarded apply reporting 32 changes, with kind
GLOBAL, name, size, section `.data`, file stubs/goldtl/symbol_stubs.c and no storage kind, backing or link symbol; sizes
are four except 0x699396 at two. The seven are 0x68a9cc, 0x699396, 0x6a2574, 0x6a4758, 0x6a4760, 0x6a9b90 and 0x6b5df0;
the twenty-five all-zero ones are 0x67bbfc, 0x67bc00, 0x67bc0c, 0x67bc10, 0x67fbb0, 0x6a3764, 0x6a3768, 0x6a9b94,
0x6ad580, 0x6ad628, 0x6ad62c, 0x6b5c2c, 0x6b5c30, 0x6b5c48, 0x6b5c4c, 0x6b5c50, 0x6b5c54, 0x6b5c58, 0x6b5c5c,
0x6b5c80, 0x6b5c84, 0x6b5c88, 0x6b5cb4, 0x6b5d08 and 0x6b5de4. Readback matched all 32 rows with every declaration size

6137d5280f2af4c72e7806b7a1578bacd8d9b04662590a9b3f9fc59c849d2558.
Layout is unchanged by the six size edits. The stub translation unit compiled with its project flags keeps object `.bss` at

source file. Lint reports no errors and the same two pre-existing warnings, with no new size, overlap or stale-evidence
