Three caveats are owed. The six stub edits are provisional until the generator is regenerated. Four callers still spell a
scalar extern of the smaller size, 0x699396, 0x6a2574, 0x6a4758 and 0x6a4760, where the element type is unchanged and only
the head element is used, so their declarations understate the object until those four function files are edited. And the
reference order of the three counters at 0x68a9d0, 0x68a9d4 and 0x68a9d8 is not resolvable from bytes because all three are
-1, so only their occupancy is proved.

## 2026-11-03 — d2 row: unsigned guard and the size premise corrected

`0x4DA690` moves from 1488 to 1489 with object 7020 against native 7057, 73 relocations, frame 0x900, equal prefix 0x31f
and lint clean. One line was kept: `if (*(unsigned char*)((char*)a0 + 0x30))` became
`if (0u < (unsigned int)*(unsigned char*)((char*)a0 + 0x30))`, because native's 0x34c is `test al,al; jbe` and this
compiler emits `jbe` only for an unsigned positive test, confirmed with a four-guard probe.
The earlier 538-byte deficit premise is stale and is corrected by measuring the landed object with `rebrew diff` alignment:
the prefix from 0 to 0x31f is native 799 against 796, the region 0x31f to 0x757 is 1080 against 1047 for minus 33, the
per-row scene pass from 0x757 to 0x1165 is 2574 against 2577 for plus 3, the second packet pass from 0x1165 to 0x1b09 is
2468 against 2509 for plus 41, and the epilogue from 0x1b09 to 0x1b91 is 136 against 91 for minus 45, giving minus 37 in
total. So the per-row pass is three bytes over rather than short, and the call sequences are identical on both sides at 223
calls in one-to-one correspondence, which means no native block and no callee is missing; the deficit is the pre-pass
region at minus 33, the second pass at plus 41 and the tail at minus 45, the last being the fourteen-argument escape block
native does not have.
The prefix stops at 0x31f because of scalar frame slots: the first mismatch is the displacement of native's
`mov [esp+0x2c],ebp` for `s2C = 0`, and every mismatch to about 0x47e is a scalar slot, with native s2C at 0x2c, s34 at
0x38, s38 at 0x24, s44 at 0x44, s30 at 0x20, s20 at 0x40 and s28 at 0x28 against this build's 0x10, 0x38, 0x28, 0x14,
0x40, 0x58 and 0x34. Slots are not declaration-order controllable, since reordering all sixty scalar declarations into
native slot order produced a byte-identical text section: the allocator state is a whole-function liveness result, so slots
follow only once the body is otherwise identical. The escape block cannot be dropped either, as that collapses the frame
and code to 6528 bytes with prefix 0x2.
Three attempts were measured and reverted. Dropping the escape block gives object 6528 and prefix 0x2. Ordering all sixty
scalars in native order changes no byte. Hoisting `if (s1C == 0) break` out of the per-row loop as
`if (s1C != 0) do { ... } while (...)` is the correct source shape, since native tests s1C once at 0x773 and back-edges to
0x77f, and it lands eight bytes from 7057, but it moves every scalar slot and costs 92 matched bytes, so it is parked at
.scratch/4da690/r13/e4_loop.c for the round that solves slots. Two native blocks the source still expresses differently
are unported: the prologue count handling, where native stores the count to slot 0x44 twice at 0x348 and 0x375 while the
source keeps a separate `k`, and `s00 = &mid[0x3c]`, which native keeps in slot 0x10 against this build's 0x14, plus the
extra `mov ebp,edx; jmp` loop entry. Kept copy at .scratch/4da690/r13/r13_final_1489.c with notes in r13_NOTES.md.

## 2026-11-03 — d2 row: slots are not addressable and the loop shape was misread

`0x4DA690` keeps 1489 at object 7020 with prefix 0x31f and an unchanged source; three findings change the plan for this
row. First, slot layout is not addressable and therefore cannot be iterated: probes in .scratch/4da690/r14 where one int
declaration list is reversed, where eight separate int statements are reversed, and where the same declarations keep their
order but the assignment order swaps show the first two compile to byte-identical text while only the assignment-order
change differs, so stack slots follow the generated body alone. Reordering all sixty declarations is the same negative and
adding locals moves the frame instead, with two addressed ints taking the prefix to 0x2, so "iterate the scalar set with
the frame held at 0x900" has no lever: a slot moves only when the whole function's liveness moves. Second, the count
handling was already native: keeping the count in s44 and dropping `k` produces an object byte-identical to the baseline,
and native storing the count to one slot twice at 0x348 and 0x375 matches the object storing at 0x348 and 0x378, so the
earlier claim of a second slot is not in the object and the item is closed. Third, the row's loop shape is already native's
and the e4 variant is the wrong shape: native's per-row back edge is `jl 0x4dae03`, offset 0x773, which is the s1C load
and test, while 0x77f is the body entry rather than a branch target, and the object back-edges to its own s1C load and test
at 0x788. Both test s1C on every row, so `if (s1C == 0) break;` at the top of the do loop is correct and the e4 hoist
contradicts native; e4 also costs 92 matched bytes and improves the slot-blind body score only from 1314 to 1317 aligned
instructions, so it was reverted.
Sizes bracket the target without prefix growth: the baseline is 7020, e4 is 7065 and a variant that recomputes `s00` at the
head without the incremental add is 7049, with native 7057 between the last two; all failed the keep rule and were
reverted, with that variant kept at .scratch/4da690/r14/c3_loop_recompute_s00.c. The slot-blind score shows where the body
really differs: 1975 native instructions against 1972 in the object with shape similarity 0.666 and 1314 aligned, and all
large gaps sit in the second packet pass, where native 0x170a to 0x1892 of 113 instructions has 1 in the object, the
object's 0x15c7 to 0x17bd of 138 has none in native, native 0x1668 to 0x16fc of 40 is missing, the object's 0x148c to
0x1595 of 70 is extra and native 0x1995 to 0x1a50 of 51 has 1. That region therefore does not merely run 41 bytes over;
it holds two relocated blocks of roughly 110 instructions, and the epilogue figure is polluted by the escape block at
object 0x1b01 to 0x1b63 which native has nowhere. The next round should drive the body to native shape and stop chasing
slots, since the prefix only moves once the allocator sees a near-native body, and should use the slot-blind score as its
metric rather than the prefix. Tools added: fslots.py to list every reference to one folded frame slot, slotmap.py to learn
the object-to-native slot map from a shape-blind alignment, and score.py to print the slot-blind body score with its
mismatched regions.

## 2026-11-03 — d2 row: the block relocation premise is an alignment artifact

`0x4DA690` keeps 1489 at object 7020 with frame 0x900 and an unchanged source, and the score to beat is a mismatch of
1329 giving shape 0.663 with 1309 aligned instructions out of 1975 native and 1972 object instructions. The previous
round's region list reproduces exactly only when general-purpose registers are folded before diffing, which yields native
0x170a with 113 instructions against the object's 0x18f1 with 1, a deleted native block at 0x1668 of 40 instructions, an
inserted object block at 0x15c7 of 138 and a native 0x1995 block of 51; with the score canonicalisation that is
register-sensitive, the same code aligns as many small opcodes. A content check settles it: the candidate's second-pass
scan `push #12de` sits at 0x168e against native's 0x171b, a delta of 0x8d, and the apparently missing native 0x1668 to
0x16fc block is the candidate's 0x15c7 to 0x1644 block, with `push eax`, call, `push #3e8`, and `cmp eax,#-1`
identically shaped. Mnemonic-only alignment gives shape 0.875 with a single gap, the known object-only escape block at
0x1b01 to 0x1b62 of 35 instructions, so no statements are relocated or missing and there is only drift.
The real cause is push-depth drift. The score folds slots relative to minus four times the push depth, and the depth
diverges at the vote and packet pass and never returns: an aligned block at native 0x00e8c has depth 14 against the
object's 4, and by the count-is-zero and count-greater-than-one bodies it is 29 against 16, a delta of 13. From that point
every scaled slot token differs, which is exactly what appeared as the 138-instruction insert and 113-instruction delete.
Native also keeps roughly 0x140 bytes more code before the second pass than the object, which supplies the offset shift.
Four experiments were discarded with the source restored and the score unchanged at 1329: the parked
c3_loop_recompute_s00 variant gives 1977 object bytes and 7055 with a mismatch of 1496, worse alignment and closer size;
rewriting the initialisation loop at source lines 211 to 219 as one stepped base with `pb += 0x35c/4` and negative indexed
access to match native's single-base form gives 1984 at 7039 and a mismatch of 1341; declaring sDC as `unsigned char` in
both positions changes object bytes but leaves the score at 1329; and removing the synthetic escape block at source lines
818 to 823 gives 1828 object bytes at 6527 with a mismatch of 1314 and shape 0.654, worse because the denominator shrinks.
Two concrete leads were measured for the next attempt. Native's packet struct at &sD8 is an int at [esp+0xf4], a hole at
[esp+0xf8], then ints at 0xfc, 0x100 and 0x104, plus a byte store at [esp+0xf0], while the source lays out five contiguous
ints so fcn_004e51d0 receives a 0x10-byte object where native passes 0x14. And the push depth first diverges between
native 0xbd9 and 0xe8c. No source shape was established for either, and the hole cannot be produced by a plain unused
local because the compiler drops it. Tools in .scratch/4da690/r15/ with rep.py for merged regions, shift.py for the
drift, pdrift.py for push-depth drift, rb.py for the register-folded dump and side.py for the pair view.

## 2026-11-03 — text reader: uninitialised index repaired at match cost

`0x42BF20` now measures 1232 of 5919 with object 5919 against native 5840, 234 relocations, status SIZE_MISMATCH and
lint clean. The edit is a correctness repair, not a match gain: the third "String too long in file %s in line %i"
diagnostic at source line 335 indexed `inc[v30]` where `v30` is declared at line 76 and never assigned anywhere, which
the compiler flags as C4700 and which would read a garbage index at runtime. The target indexes `inc[v2c]` at all four
sites, at 0x42d160, 0x42d22c, 0x42d278 and 0x42d2c4, each loading v2c and shifting eight over the inc base. The index is
corrected to `inc[v2c]` and the dead `int v30;` declaration removed. The repair costs 29 matched bytes and adds 52 object
bytes, because dropping the only read of v30 removes that stack slot and shifts every later offset, taking the object from
5867 to 5919; it is kept because an uninitialised memory read is not an acceptable trade for matched bytes.
Measurement caveat: this row's reported match moved from 1420 at session start to 1261 before this edit with a
byte-identical text section, because other sessions changed managed relocation bindings and the relocation count fell from
276 to 232, so a deterministic local metric was pinned instead, with the text at 5872 before the repair for plus 32 over
native, 307 equal bytes outside relocation spans out of 4660, and the first divergence at offset 1. An audit found no other
defect: the prologue and epilogue, the check-stack frame with four saved registers and the early-return block, the
zero-initialisation group order with the 0x149d120 walk, all seven memset sizes and their order, both parse passes with
their directive handling and sprintf forms, the comma list loop with its 0x4800000 and 0x1000 split, the ';', '+' and '_'
cases with their tables and record strides, the write sequence with all eight calls in native argument order, the third
pass header and the success and failure epilogues were all checked instruction by instruction against the listing and
found faithful, including the 0x4800000 index built as `shl edi,0x17` through `lea edx,[edx+edx*8]` which is faithful
rather than defective.
The remaining wall is stack-slot allocation, not C semantics: native's frame is exactly the sum of its declared locals with
fifteen int scalars from 0x10 to 0x48 giving 0xeb6c, while this source compiles to fourteen int slots giving 0xeb68, so
starts[] sits at 0x48 against native's 0x4c and every array base is four bytes low, with the scalar permutation differing
as well, v18 at 0x28 against native's 0x18 and ebx chosen as the zero register where native picks ebp. Forcing a fifteenth
slot by initialising v30 or by declaring a volatile length left the frame at 0xeb68, so the slot is not reproducible from
source form. Drift windows from `rebrew diagnose drift` are 511 to 516 and 632 to 664 at minus 13, and 3963 to 3971 at
minus 48. Every direct callee resolves to a project file or to the linked CRT, so the unresolved part is names rather than
bodies, and no prototype was speculative. Instruments in .scratch/ with score.py, esp4.py, shape.py, mk.sh and the target
assembly dump.
